# Host adapter contract

The refinement skill is host-agnostic. It operates on a hosted Product Change through a host adapter supplied by the active product workflow.

The adapter must make these facts discoverable before the interview starts:

- how to identify and read the same draft change across sessions;
- where the accepted product definition lives and how to validate it;
- how to inspect an artifact, its graph neighbours, relationships and impact polarity;
- where the change's working memory, rationale, open questions, exclusions and proposed artifacts are persisted;
- how to validate the proposed change as an overlay without touching accepted product truth;
- which separate host actions approve, apply or archive the change.

The skill may use host-specific names, paths and commands only through that adapter context. Those details are implementation of the host, not part of the refinement contract.

The adapter must preserve these invariants:

- refinement resumes the same change rather than creating a second lifecycle;
- graph results are evidence and recommendations, never authority to widen scope or edit artifacts;
- persistence is limited to the draft change and its working memory;
- validation is deterministic and non-mutating;
- refinement cannot approve, apply or archive.

When no adapter is available, ask the user to select a supported product workflow instead of guessing a storage format or inventing a lifecycle.
